title: Linux syscall table (x86-64)
summary: The Linux syscall table maps syscall numbers to kernel functions. On x86-64, the syscall number is passed in RAX, arguments in RDI, RSI, RDX, R10, R8, R9. The kernel returns the result in RAX (negative errno on error). Key syscalls: 0 read, 1 write, 2 open, 3 close, 4 stat, 5 fstat, 6 lstat, 7 poll, 8 lseek, 9 mmap, 10 mprotect, 11 munmap, 12 brk, 13 rt_sigaction, 14 rt_sigprocmask, 15 rt_sigreturn, 16 ioctl, 17 pread64, 18 pwrite64, 19 readv, 20 writev, 21 access, 22 pipe, 23 select, 24 sched_yield, 25 mremap, 32 dup, 33 dup2, 35 nanosleep, 39 getpid, 41 socket, 42 connect, 43 accept, 44 sendto, 45 recvfrom, 46 sendmsg, 47 recvmsg, 49 bind, 50 listen, 51 getsockname, 52 getpeername, 56 clone, 57 fork, 58 vfork, 59 execve, 60 exit, 61 wait4, 62 kill, 72 fcntl, 78 getdents, 79 getcwd, 80 chdir, 83 mkdir, 84 rmdir, 85 creat, 86 link, 87 unlink, 89 readlink, 90 chmod, 92 chown, 96 gettimeofday, 97 getrlimit, 102 getuid, 104 getgid, 105 setuid, 107 setgid, 108 geteuid, 110 getegid, 124 sched_getparam, 158 arch_prctl, 202 futex, 203 sched_setaffinity, 217 getdents64, 228 clock_gettime, 231 exit_group, 232 epoll_wait, 233 epoll_ctl, 234 tgkill, 257 openat, 262 newfstatat, 269 eventfd, 270 fallocate, 271 timerfd_create, 272 eventfd2, 273 epoll_create1, 274 dup3, 275 pipe2, 281 epoll_pwait, 288 accept4, 290 recvmmsg, 291 fanotify_init, 292 fanotify_mark, 293 prlimit64, 299 recvmmsg, 302 prlimit64, 318 getrandom, 319 memfd_create, 322 execveat, 323 userfaultfd, 332 statx, 334 pidfd_send_signal, 434 pidfd_open, 435 clone3, 436 close_range, 437 openat2, 438 pidfd_getfd, 439 faccessat2, 440 process_madvise, 441 epoll_pwait2, 442 mount_setattr, 443 quotactl_fd, 444 landlock_create_ruleset, 445 landlock_add_rule, 446 landlock_restrict_self, 447 memfd_secret, 448 process_mrelease, 449 futex_waitv, 450 set_mempolicy_home_node, 451 cachestat, 452 fchmodat2, 453 map_shadow_stack, 454 futex_wake, 455 futex_wait, 456 futex_requeue, 457 statmount, 458 listmount, 459 mount_setattr, 460 cache (statx), etc.

structure.meaning: The syscall number is passed in RAX (x86-64). On ARM64, it's X8. On RISC-V, it's a7.

structure.size: RDI, RSI, RDX, R10, R8, R9
structure.meaning: Up to 6 arguments in registers (x86-64). Additional args on stack.
Success: non-negative result. Error: negative errno (-1 to -4095).
SYSCALL (0x0F 0x05) on x86-64. SVC #0 on ARM64. ECALL on RISC-V.
Virtual Dynamic Shared Object: provides fast userspace implementations of gettimeofday, clock_gettime, getcpu, etc. (avoids syscall overhead).
Syscall filtering via seccomp-BPF. Can allow, deny, or trap syscalls.

notes: The syscall table is defined in arch/x86/entry/syscalls/syscall_64.tbl.
Syscall numbers are stable (never reused) for backward compatibility.
New syscalls are added at the end of the table.
The vDSO (virtual DSO) provides fast userspace implementations of common syscalls.
seccomp-BPF can filter syscalls per-process for sandboxing.
